title: Third-Person -s / -es Spelling Rules
description: Master the spelling rules for he/she/it verb forms: -s, -es, -ies, and irregulars.
objectives: Add -es correctly to verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -z, and -o
Apply the consonant + y -> -ies rule accurately in verbs like 'study' and 'carry'
Identify key irregular third-person verbs (have -> has, go -> goes, do -> does)

vocabularyList.definition: To look at or observe attentively over a period of time.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He watches the evening news every day.

vocabularyList.definition: To impart knowledge to or instruct someone.
To clean with water and typically soap or detergent.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He washes his car on Saturdays.

vocabularyList.definition: To repair or mend something that is broken.
To move from one place to another; travel.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: She goes to the gym three times a week.

vocabularyList.definition: To perform or carry out an action or task.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He does his homework before dinner.

vocabularyList.definition: To move through the air using wings or an aircraft.
To support and move someone or something from one place to another.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: She carries a heavy bag of books.

vocabularyList.definition: To shed tears, typically as an expression of pain or sorrow.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The baby cries when he is hungry.

vocabularyList.definition: To intercept and hold something moving through the air.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: He catches the morning train at 8:00.

sections.title: Spelling Transformations for He, She, and It
sections.content: When the subject is **he**, **she**, or **it**, we must modify the verb. While most verbs simply add **-s**, English phonetic rules require special spelling endings.

tables.title: Crucial Form / Use / Common Mistakes
rows: Apply exact rule according to spelling
He watches TV / She studies law

callouts.title: Vowel + Y Alert
callouts.text: Remember: 'play' -> 'plays' (vowel a + y); 'study' -> 'studies' (consonant d + y). Only change the y when a consonant comes before it!

callouts.title: Irregular 'Have'
callouts.text: The verb 'have' becomes **has** with he/she/it: 'She **has** a car' (never 'She haves').

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: General rule: Add -s (eat -> eats, read -> reads).
Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -z: Add -es (watches, washes, kisses, fixes).
Consonant + y: Change y to -ies (study -> studies, carry -> carries).
Vowel + y: Just add -s (play -> plays, buy -> buys).
